title: Visium HD Spatial Gene Expression Protocol: Library Preparation and Analysis
author: Gurveer Gill

steps.title: Tissue Preparation and Imaging
steps.instruction: Prepare tissue samples and capture morphology before transfer to Visium HD slides.

substeps.instruction: Section tissue samples to 5 µm thickness and mount onto plain glass slides.
Perform deparaffinization and H&E staining.
Capture tissue morphology using the Olympus VS110 Slide Scanner microscope at 40× magnification.

steps.title: Visium HD Slide Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare Visium HD slides for tissue placement.

substeps.instruction: Thaw, wash, and equilibrate Visium HD slides using the manufacturer’s recommended buffers.

steps.title: Tissue Transfer and Library Construction
steps.instruction: Transfer analytes and construct libraries using specific probe panels.

substeps.instruction: Transfer tissue analytes from the glass slide to the Visium HD capture areas using the CytAssist instrument.
Prepare tissues using the Visium HD Spatial Gene Expression Kit with the human probe panel plus the custom GCAR1 probe panel addon.
Perform probe extension and library construction as described in Visium HD User Guides CG000684 and CG000685.

steps.title: Sequencing and FASTQ Generation
steps.instruction: Sequence libraries on an Illumina NextSeq 2000 and generate FASTQ files.

substeps.instruction: Set cycle settings: Read 1 (43 cycles), i7 index (10 cycles), i5 index (10 cycles), and Read 2 (50 cycles).
Generate FASTQ files onboard using Dragen BCL Convert v4.2.7.

steps.title: Reference Genome Generation and Alignment
steps.instruction: Create a custom reference and align sequencing data.

substeps.instruction: Generate a custom reference genome using spaceranger mkref (Space Ranger v3.0.1), incorporating human GRCh38 (GENCODE v32/Ensembl98) and full GCAR1 construct sequences.
Align FASTQ files and perform automated image detection/alignment using spaceranger count (Space Ranger v3.0.1 for ASPS-01 xenograft; v4.0.1 for ASPS-02 biopsies).
Aggregate data to 24 µm bins.

steps.title: Initial Data Processing in Seurat
steps.instruction: Process binned data using Seurat (v5.3.1) to identify clusters.

substeps.instruction: Normalize data with NormalizeData().
Select variable features with FindVariableFeatures().
Scale data with ScaleData().
Run Principal Component Analysis with RunPCA().
Cluster bins using FindNeighbors() and FindClusters().
Exclude low-quality clusters (e.g., regions of hemorrhage or bins outside tissue) based on low gene counts.

steps.title: Cell Type Deconvolution and Program Derivation
steps.instruction: Perform unsupervised deconvolution to identify cell types and expression programs.

substeps.instruction: Identify over-dispersed genes per sample using STdeconvolve (v1.3.1) with the function restrictCorpus(removeAbove = 1.0, removeBelow = 0.01, alpha = 0.05).
Input results to consensus Non-negative Matrix Factorization (cNMF) via the mosaicMPI package to derive expression programs and quantify relative usage across bins.
Annotate programs using established reference marker genes and perform pathway enrichment analysis with g:Profiler.

steps.title: Niche Identification and Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze 24 µm bin data in Seurat (v5.3.1) to identify and characterize T-cell niches.

substeps.instruction: Merge samples with merge(), join layers with JoinLayers(), and filter for bins with non-zero counts using subset(SeuratObject, nCount_Spatial.024um > 0).
Extract spatial bin coordinates with seurat_object_coords() and identify neighbors using custom program_neighbours() functions.
Restrict analysis to bins with non-infinite normalized program usage.
Identify T-cell niches (bins of interest, BOI) as bins positive for a T-cell program (usage ≥ 0.05).
Binarize program usage values (≥ 0.05 = 1, else 0).
For each BOI and its neighbouring bins (radius up to 3), calculate mean binarized program usage and visualize with ComplexHeatmap (v2.15.3).
Split the column dendrogram to define distinct niches, assign labels, and visualize with Seurat’s DotPlot() function.
Calculate the percent of bins expressing specific genes of interest per niche.

steps.title: Statistical Analysis of Niches
steps.instruction: Perform statistical tests on niche contingency tables and gene expression.

substeps.instruction: Perform statistical analyses on contingency tables using Fisher’s Exact Test (fisher.test() from base R stats v4.3.1) and post-hoc pairwise comparisons with pairwise_fisher_test() from rstatix (v0.7.3).
For T cell-specific gene expression: subset bins expressing any of CD3D, CD3E, CD3G, CD8A, or GCAR.
Classify neighbouring bins (radii 0–3) as “inside” or “outside” the T-cell radius.
Compare average expression of genes of interest using Student’s t-test via compare_means() from ggpubr (v0.6.2) and visualize with ggplot2 (v3.5.2).
Perform differential gene expression on pseudobulked bins using ALDEx2 (v1.32.0) with the call: aldex(mc.samples=128, test="t", effect=TRUE, denom="iVha", verbose=FALSE, paired.test=FALSE).
